response.reason: NL1 establishes root-level power-on initial entry into Operate and introduces the substates Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking as members reachable within Operate (context for later segment). NL2 establishes two bidirectional-style transition endpoints for start/keyOff signals at the root/system scope (on -> Operate via start, Operate -> off/root via keyOff), each with its own event trigger. NL3 establishes that within Operate, the system transitions between substates depending on actions (accelerating, braking, stopping) - this is a broad capability statement providing the shared owner context (Operate) for substates named in NL1, but does not itself give exact source/target pairs beyond what NL1 already introduces the substate list; treat as context establishing owner, plus containment of substates under Operate, since NL1 explicitly names these substates as things within Operate's scope (per NL3's "Within Operate... substates"). I extract: (1) NL1: initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (1b) NL1: containment of Idle, Accelerating/Cruising(interpreted as two names: Accelerating and Cruising), Braking within Operate; (2) NL2: transition_endpoints for start signal (source=off/root, target=Operate) and keyOff signal (source=Operate, target=off/root), each as separate endpoint contracts with trigger info in transition_groups; (3) NL3 is largely context/broad-capability without exact source-target pairs, but establishes containment already captured; mark NL3 as context since it doesn't add a new independently gradable obligation beyond restating substate transition capability already covered by NL1's naming and containment. I avoid manufacturing progress/state_action contracts since no explicit continuous/repeated obligation phrase appears (transitions "based on user actions" is not itself a continuous task obligation). I preserve Accelerating and Cruising as two distinct named states per "Accelerating or Cruising" phrasing (alternative reading: could be one combined mode name, preserved as alternative_reading is not applicable since this is not cardinality, but I add a containment contract for each of Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking to preserve independent violability, and use their combined naming faithfully as quoted "Accelerating or Cruising" only where relevant).

arguments.reason: NL1 establishes root-level power-on initial entry into Operate and introduces the substates Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking as members reachable within Operate (context for later segment). NL2 establishes two bidirectional-style transition endpoints for start/keyOff signals at the root/system scope (on -> Operate via start, Operate -> off/root via keyOff), each with its own event trigger. NL3 establishes that within Operate, the system transitions between substates depending on actions (accelerating, braking, stopping) - this is a broad capability statement providing the shared owner context (Operate) for substates named in NL1, but does not itself give exact source/target pairs beyond what NL1 already introduces the substate list; treat as context establishing owner, plus containment of substates under Operate, since NL1 explicitly names these substates as things within Operate's scope (per NL3's "Within Operate... substates"). I extract: (1) NL1: initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (1b) NL1: containment of Idle, Accelerating/Cruising(interpreted as two names: Accelerating and Cruising), Braking within Operate; (2) NL2: transition_endpoints for start signal (source=off/root, target=Operate) and keyOff signal (source=Operate, target=off/root), each as separate endpoint contracts with trigger info in transition_groups; (3) NL3 is largely context/broad-capability without exact source-target pairs, but establishes containment already captured; mark NL3 as context since it doesn't add a new independently gradable obligation beyond restating substate transition capability already covered by NL1's naming and containment. I avoid manufacturing progress/state_action contracts since no explicit continuous/repeated obligation phrase appears (transitions "based on user actions" is not itself a continuous task obligation). I preserve Accelerating and Cruising as two distinct named states per "Accelerating or Cruising" phrasing (alternative reading: could be one combined mode name, preserved as alternative_reading is not applicable since this is not cardinality, but I add a containment contract for each of Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking to preserve independent violability, and use their combined naming faithfully as quoted "Accelerating or Cruising" only where relevant).

response.reason: Applying contract-structure/contrastive audit across the source PlantUML/inventory and closed FCSTM for the power-cycle model. Key findings: (1) root/system power-on initial entry contract (REF-001) targets Operate; the closed model has [*]->PoweredOn->Operate via start, which is the correct owner-local chain, so it is satisfied and omitted. (2) NL2 endpoint contracts describe start (root->Operate) and keyOff (Operate->root) transitions; the closed model instead realizes start as PoweredOn->Operate (an intermediate state, not literally 'root/system power-off scope'), and keyOff as Idle/AccelOrCruising/Braking -> [*] with an effect-token, gated by a separate guarded Operate->[*] transition on R45RouteToken==10, which is a structurally different, indirect path than a direct Operate-to-root edge with a keyOff trigger. This is a wrong-target/mismatched structural discrepancy worth flagging for REF-007 (keyOff endpoint), since the exact edge carrying trigger keyOff targets an internal pseudo-state routed through a guarded intermediary rather than terminating directly, and the direct source-modeled edge 'Operate -> [*] : keyOff' (tr_0010) was compiled into this two-stage macro. Per macro-boundary discipline, source_trace maps tr_0010 to macro members (transition_segment:tr_0010:segment:1..4), which correspond to lines 19,20,21,24 (three keyOff edges from substates plus the guarded Operate->[*] edge). This is a complete macro closing the original single authored edge, so it should not be treated as violation without further evidence; I treat this as satisfied per macro discipline and omit it. (3) NL1-CONTAIN-1..4 containment obligations for Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking under Operate: the exact source inventory only declares 3 direct children of Operate (Idle, AcceleratingOrCruising, Braking) — 'Accelerating' and 'Cruising' are collapsed into one single child state 'AcceleratingOrCruising' in both source and FCSTM. This means the NL's distinct Accelerating and Cruising obligations (CONTAIN-2, CONTAIN-3) are not independently satisfied: only one merged substate exists, which is a structural collapse of two required substates into one, a violation of the distinct-containment obligation for each of Accelerating and Cruising individually. NL-CONTRACT-NL1-CONTAIN-4 (Braking) and CONTAIN-1 (Idle) are satisfied by exact source_id Operate.Idle / Operate.Braking and model refs state:Idle:line:9 / state:Braking:line:11. (4) Cardinality contract (REF-009) must be given exactly one binding row: NL states three named groups (Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking) as explicit_named_members under Operate, but the closed inventory only shows 3 direct children (not 4), which is itself the same collapse issue projected into cardinality rather than a new structural claim.

result.reason: Two containment obligations (i0, i1) both concern the NL phrase 'Accelerating or Cruising': the source and closed model consistently show a single merged state AcceleratingOrCruising under Operate, with no independently modeled Accelerating or Cruising state anywhere. This is a genuine two-reading ambiguity (single combined disjunctive state vs. two independently required substates) that the supplied facts cannot resolve either way, so both remain unresolved undercutting readings. The keyOff-endpoint obligation (i2) shows an established two-step guard-conditioned realization whose completion depends on an SMT guard with solver_status=not_run; the macro/segment evidence is a plausible but unconfirmed rebuttal, so this stays established with a surviving undercutting defeater given the unresolved guard satisfiability. The start-transition obligation (i3) was explicitly left unresolved by the grounding lens over whether 'root scope' denotes the wrapper, PoweredOn, or an abstract off-condition; this is a genuine unresolved ambiguity, not an established violation. The cardinality obligation (i4) is squarely established: exact source and model inventories both show exactly 3 direct children under Operate against the NL requirement's primary reading of 4, and the 'Accelerating or Cruising' merged label is only a competing reading, which the dossier itself frames as an undercutting alternative that survives (two readings: 3 real children vs. possible different member-domain interpretation), keeping this D1-worthy through an undercutting-survives defeater rather than clean established-with-no-defeater, since the merged-label alternative is a competent alternative reading of scope. contract_extraction.reason: NL1 establishes root-level power-on initial entry into Operate and introduces the substates Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking as members reachable within Operate (context for later segment). NL2 establishes two bidirectional-style transition endpoints for start/keyOff signals at the root/system scope (on -> Operate via start, Operate -> off/root via keyOff), each with its own event trigger. NL3 establishes that within Operate, the system transitions between substates depending on actions (accelerating, braking, stopping) - this is a broad capability statement providing the shared owner context (Operate) for substates named in NL1, but does not itself give exact source/target pairs beyond what NL1 already introduces the substate list; treat as context establishing owner, plus containment of substates under Operate, since NL1 explicitly names these substates as things within Operate's scope (per NL3's "Within Operate... substates"). I extract: (1) NL1: initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (1b) NL1: containment of Idle, Accelerating/Cruising(interpreted as two names: Accelerating and Cruising), Braking within Operate; (2) NL2: transition_endpoints for start signal (source=off/root, target=Operate) and keyOff signal (source=Operate, target=off/root), each as separate endpoint contracts with trigger info in transition_groups; (3) NL3 is largely context/broad-capability without exact source-target pairs, but establishes containment already captured; mark NL3 as context since it doesn't add a new independently gradable obligation beyond restating substate transition capability already covered by NL1's naming and containment. I avoid manufacturing progress/state_action contracts since no explicit continuous/repeated obligation phrase appears (transitions "based on user actions" is not itself a continuous task obligation). I preserve Accelerating and Cruising as two distinct named states per "Accelerating or Cruising" phrasing (alternative reading: could be one combined mode name, preserved as alternative_reading is not applicable since this is not cardinality, but I add a containment contract for each of Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking to preserve independent violability, and use their combined naming faithfully as quoted "Accelerating or Cruising" only where relevant).

branches.reason: Applying contract-structure/contrastive audit across the source PlantUML/inventory and closed FCSTM for the power-cycle model. Key findings: (1) root/system power-on initial entry contract (REF-001) targets Operate; the closed model has [*]->PoweredOn->Operate via start, which is the correct owner-local chain, so it is satisfied and omitted. (2) NL2 endpoint contracts describe start (root->Operate) and keyOff (Operate->root) transitions; the closed model instead realizes start as PoweredOn->Operate (an intermediate state, not literally 'root/system power-off scope'), and keyOff as Idle/AccelOrCruising/Braking -> [*] with an effect-token, gated by a separate guarded Operate->[*] transition on R45RouteToken==10, which is a structurally different, indirect path than a direct Operate-to-root edge with a keyOff trigger. This is a wrong-target/mismatched structural discrepancy worth flagging for REF-007 (keyOff endpoint), since the exact edge carrying trigger keyOff targets an internal pseudo-state routed through a guarded intermediary rather than terminating directly, and the direct source-modeled edge 'Operate -> [*] : keyOff' (tr_0010) was compiled into this two-stage macro. Per macro-boundary discipline, source_trace maps tr_0010 to macro members (transition_segment:tr_0010:segment:1..4), which correspond to lines 19,20,21,24 (three keyOff edges from substates plus the guarded Operate->[*] edge). This is a complete macro closing the original single authored edge, so it should not be treated as violation without further evidence; I treat this as satisfied per macro discipline and omit it. stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes root-level power-on initial entry into Operate and introduces the substates Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking as members reachable within Operate (context for later segment). NL2 establishes two bidirectional-style transition endpoints for start/keyOff signals at the root/system scope (on -> Operate via start, Operate -> off/root via keyOff), each with its own event trigger. NL3 establishes that within Operate, the system transitions between substates depending on actions (accelerating, braking, stopping) - this is a broad capability statement providing the shared owner context (Operate) for substates named in NL1, but does not itself give exact source/target pairs beyond what NL1 already introduces the substate list; treat as context establishing owner, plus containment of substates under Operate, since NL1 explicitly names these substates as things within Operate's scope (per NL3's "Within Operate... substates"). I extract: (1) NL1: initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (1b) NL1: containment of Idle, Accelerating/Cruising(interpreted as two names: Accelerating and Cruising), Braking within Operate; (2) NL2: transition_endpoints for start signal (source=off/root, target=Operate) and keyOff signal (source=Operate, target=off/root), each as separate endpoint contracts with trigger info in transition_groups; (3) NL3 is largely context/broad-capability without exact source-target pairs, but establishes containment already captured; mark NL3 as context since it doesn't add a new independently gradable obligation beyond restating substate transition capability already covered by NL1's naming and containment. I avoid manufacturing progress/state_action contracts since no explicit continuous/repeated obligation phrase appears (transitions "based on user actions" is not itself a continuous task obligation). I preserve Accelerating and Cruising as two distinct named states per "Accelerating or Cruising" phrasing (alternative reading: could be one combined mode name, preserved as alternative_reading is not applicable since this is not cardinality, but I add a containment contract for each of Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking to preserve independent violability, and use their combined naming faithfully as quoted "Accelerating or Cruising" only where relevant).
